root_cause.text: The mana_ib_install_cq_cb() function in the RDMA/mana driver failed to validate that a CQ was already in use by another WQ, allowing user-space to specify multiple WQs sharing the same CQ, which triggered a WARN_ON() that did not prevent execution, leading to kernel corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces the `WARN_ON(gc->cq_table[cq->queue.id])` with an explicit `if (gc->cq_table[cq->queue.id]) return -EINVAL;`, and the commit message states that "the user can specify WQs sharing the same CQ ... this will trigger the WARN_ON() then go on to corrupt the kernel. Just reject it outright and fail the QP creation." The added comment also confirms "sharing a CQ between WQs is not supported".

Just reject it outright and fail the QP creation." The added comment also confirms "sharing a CQ between WQs is not supported".

candidates.rationale: This check validates the CQ ID range but does not check if the CQ slot is already occupied, missing a crucial validation against duplicate usage.
Returning an error when the ID is out of range is correct, but it does not address the case of a valid but already-in-use CQ ID.
This WARN_ON is the only check for an already-used CQ, but it does not prevent execution, allowing the driver to proceed with reassigning the same CQ to another WQ, leading to kernel corruption.

This conditional checks for a kernel memory buffer; although not directly related to the duplicate CQ issue, it is part of the installation path that executes without proper duplicate validation, contributing to the vulnerability's exploitation.
This assignment stores the CQ's kernel memory pointer; when executed on a duplicate CQ, it overwrites the existing entry and corrupts kernel data structures.

vuln_statements.explanation: This WARN_ON is the only check for a duplicate CQ, but it does not prevent execution, allowing the driver to proceed with reassigning the same CQ to another WQ, leading to kernel corruption.
This assignment stores the CQ's kernel memory pointer; when executed on a duplicate CQ, it overwrites the existing entry and corrupts kernel data structures.
This conditional leads to the assignment that can overwrite an existing CQ entry, contributing to the vulnerability's exploitation when duplicate CQ usage is not prevented.
